correctness.rationale: After choosing the first vertex, equality and the two ordered incidences to it identify its singleton, its own part minus itself, its outgoing part and its incoming part. With two further selections one distinguishes exactly the counts in those last three regions truncated at two. Conversely, mapping each choice to the corresponding region, reusing an image on repetitions and choosing a fresh vertex otherwise, always preserves the atomic diagram for the two remaining rounds. This argument works irrespective of the side chosen. Thus the unrooted three-round invariant is exactly the set of realizable pointed types, not their multiplicities. Independently grouping the capped words by the number of singleton parts gives 1, 2, 4, and 3 types for three, two, one, and zero singletons respectively; with one singleton the ordered pair of other sizes contributes four different directed profiles, and with zero singletons both mixed necklaces 223 and 233 give the same footprint. The all-3 footprint requires every part to have at least three vertices, giving the sharp 9 bound. The general game proof, not the finite verifier, covers all positive sizes.
residual_risks: Neither empty parts, named fibers, wider relational signatures nor graphs outside the stated family are covered.

value.rationale: For the smallest cyclic directed template the exact invariant detects the order of differently sized outgoing and incoming parts, while rank three loses exactly one distinction visible at variable width three. The uniform nine-vertex bound is sharp, and the 223/233 pair supplies a concrete boundary witness for treating depth and variable width separately. This is an exact theorem for an infinite natural family, not just the count of a finite sample.
residual_risks: The bound is internal to this family and not a size bound for arbitrary directed graphs.
